lockFileMaintenance.description: Label the weekly whole-tree refresh so it is distinguishable from a targeted update. The release-age hold is nulled here: regeneration lets npm and cargo pick transitive versions, so the hold cannot be enforced and would sit pending on nearly every run. Green required checks automerge the refresh; a red one stays open for diagnosis.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: minimumReleaseAge restates Renovate's own default for this block; without it the 3-day hold above reads as applying to security fixes.

packageRules.description: Update lockfiles within compatible cargo and npm ranges; replace ranges for incompatible releases.

Do not manage the workspace overrides block as first-class dependencies. Its entries are deliberate transitive security floors chosen for the advisory each one closes, not versions to track upstream, so a per-entry bump would raise the floor to whatever released last and drop the reason it was set. Pinned transitive versions still refresh within range through normal lockfile updates.
Hold major upgrades for dashboard approval and process them after lower-risk updates.
Pin Docker base images by digest for reproducible, tamper-evident builds.
Automerge patch, pin, and digest updates for Docker Official Images after required checks pass.
Treat GitHub-owned actions as platform dependencies and automerge patch, pin, and digest updates after required checks pass.
Automerge third-party action patch and pin updates; require manual review when a pinned tag moves to a new digest.

Exempt action digest updates from the release-age hold. The hold earns its keep against a newly published version that has not been in the wild long enough to be trusted. A digest update is not that: it re-pins an action to the commit its already-pinned major tag now names, which is the version this repo has been trusting by tag all along. Holding it only means carrying a knowingly stale pin for three days and occupying a prConcurrentLimit slot while it waits.
Automerge stable cargo and npm patch updates; keep pre-1.0 updates manual.

Keep every PostgreSQL image pin in one PR. scripts/compose-dev-invariants.sh requires docker/compose.dev.yml and the ci.yml backend service to pin the identical postgres digest, so a split across the docker-compose and github-actions managers fails the dev/CI parity gate on both branches. Grouping the CI workflow service with the compose images moves them together. The release-age hold is restated here because Renovate parses that workflow service image under the github-actions manager, so the digest exemption above would otherwise reach the CI half alone. Grouping does not wait for a member that is not yet eligible: it ships the eligible subset, which is a split by date rather than by manager and breaks the same gate.
Keep the SQLx library and migration CLI compatible.
Ignore rand_core_06 because the alias intentionally targets the 0.6 API.

These versions mirror the toolchain vite-plus bundles rather than describing independent choices, and `vp migrate` is what moves them: it re-pins vite-plus, the vite -> @voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core alias, and the vitest and @vitest/* catalog entries to whatever the new vp bundles, in one pass. Renovate cannot see a bundled version at all (`vp toolchain vitest` is the only reading of it), so an automatic bump of any member sets a number vp owns: vitest 4.1.11 against a vp bundling 4.1.10 makes `vp test --coverage` refuse to start. Dashboard approval keeps Renovate in the role it is competent for, announcing that a release exists, while the update itself is performed by running `vp migrate` and committing its result.

The generated color primitives pin these exactly; any bump fails the radix-gen drift test until `vp run primitives:gen` is rerun and the palette diff reviewed, so move them as one deliberate, dashboard-approved group.

customManagers.description: Track SQLX_CLI_VERSION because it is not embedded in an install-action tool list.

Track annotated version pins in workflows and composite action files. The first pattern matches a renovate comment above a version key; the second matches the SBOM generator, whose version and sha256 digest move together. File patterns are the customManagers:githubActionsVersions preset's verbatim, because the preset would double-claim these annotations while leaving that digest unrewritten. ARG-shaped Dockerfile pins belong to the dockerfileVersions preset in extends.
